mainTopic: Gifts with conditions and limits: a shared or gifted אתרוג, a gift on condition of return, a lifetime gift, and a gift the recipient refuses.
overview: The גמרא finishes the case of an אתרוג given 'to you, and after you to so-and-so.' Everyone agrees the first person fulfills the מצוה with it, and רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue only about selling or eating it. רבה בר רב הונא rules that a brother who uses an אתרוג bought with shared estate money fulfills the מצוה only if he may eat it, and only when every brother has an אתרוג of his own. רבא teaches that a gift on condition of return is a real gift, so it works for the מצוה if it is returned. A story about a palm tree shows that a lifetime gift meant to come back to the giver cannot be passed on to someone else. רב נחמן rules that an ox given on condition of return can be made הקדש and then returned. רבא challenges this, and רב אשי decides that it depends on whether the giver said 'return it' or 'return it to me.' Finally, שמואל and רבי יוחנן argue about whether a person acquires property written to him if he refuses it. רבי אבא בר ממל begins to explain that they do not really disagree, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why would the owner give it if it can't be used?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that the first recipient cannot fulfill his מצוה with the אתרוג, because then the gift would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he can't fulfill his מצוה with it, why did the owner give it to him at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down its own earlier suggestion that the first person cannot use the gifted אתרוג for the מצוה. An אתרוג is given precisely so that someone can do the מצוה with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier suggestion was that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about whether the first recipient fulfills the מצוה. The גמרא says that can't be right. Nobody gives someone an אתרוג for סוכות unless he means for that person to fulfill the מצוה with it. So the giver clearly meant for him to be able to use it.

keyTerms.meaning: to fulfill (literally, 'to go out of') one's obligation
he fulfills his obligation with it
for what purpose?
he gave it to him

phrases.english: If he does not fulfill his obligation with it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the first person who received the אתרוג 'for you, and after you for so-and-so.'

phrases.english: for what purpose did the owner give it to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִיפָּק לָא נָפֵיק בֵּיהּ, לְמַאי יַהֲבֵיהּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made just before this point (on the previous lines of the דף) that the מחלוקת concerns fulfilling the מצוה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is about whether the first recipient fulfills the מצוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the obvious intent of the giver. An אתרוג given at סוכות is given so the person can fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: Everyone agrees he fulfills the מצוה; the argument is about selling or eating it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves the מחלוקת. Everyone agrees the first recipient fulfills his obligation. רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only argue about a case where he sold the אתרוג or ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, about fulfilling the מצוה, everyone agrees that he fulfills it. If he sold it or ate it, that is where we reach the argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word 'אלא' (rather), the גמרא gives a new explanation of what the two תנאים actually argue about. It is not about doing the מצוה but about selling or eating the אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the אתרוג for the מצוה is clearly allowed according to everyone. The real question is how much ownership the first person has. According to רבי, the second person can take the אתרוג back from a buyer, or collect its value if the first person ate it. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first person owns it fully and owes the second person nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces a new explanation that replaces the old one)
everyone agrees (literally, 'the whole world does not argue')
he sold it or ate it
we have arrived at the argument

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of 'given to you and after you to so-and-so,' the first person can certainly fulfill the מצוה. רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only argue about whether he may sell it or eat it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי holds the first person can't use the אתרוג for the מצוה. Both agree he can. They argue only about selling or eating it.

phrases.english: Rather, with regard to fulfilling the obligation –

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי, דְּנָפֵיק בֵּיהּ;
phrases.english: everyone agrees that he fulfills his obligation with it;
if he sold it or ate it –
we have arrived at the argument between רבי
and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִיפָּק דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּנָפֵיק בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 1 rejected the old reading, this gives the corrected version of the מחלוקת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Fulfilling the מצוה is agreed upon. The מחלוקת is only about selling or eating the אתרוג.

steps.title: Brothers who bought an אתרוג with shared estate money
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules about brothers who share an inherited estate and bought an אתרוג with it. A brother who uses it fulfills the מצוה only if he is allowed to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Brothers bought an אתרוג with money from the shared estate, and one of them took it and used it for the מצוה. If he is allowed to eat it, he fulfilled the מצוה. If not, he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא brings a related ruling about an אתרוג that belongs to several brothers together. The test is whether the one using it is allowed to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אתרוג for the מצוה must belong to the person using it. If the brothers would let him eat it, they have really given up their share, so it is fully his. If they wouldn't let him eat it, it is still partly theirs, and he hasn't fulfilled the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: the shared, not-yet-divided property of an inherited estate
the brothers (here, heirs who share an estate)
he fulfilled his obligation
he is able (allowed) to eat it

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical test for when a shared אתרוג counts as 'yours': could you eat it without objection?

phrases.english: רבה בר רב הונא says:
Brothers who bought an אתרוג
with money from the shared estate;
one of them took it and fulfilled his obligation with it –
if he is able to eat it, he has fulfilled his obligation;
phrases.notes: He means: if his brothers would let him eat it, so it's really his.

phrases.english: and if not, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא הָאַחִין שֶׁקָּנוּ אֶתְרוֹג בִּתְפוּסַת הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related ruling about ownership of an אתרוג, following the discussion of the gifted אתרוג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brother who uses an אתרוג bought with shared estate money fulfills the מצוה only if he is allowed to eat it.

steps.title: Only when every brother has his own אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is limited. It applies only when each brother has an אתרוג. If the other brothers get only a quince or a pomegranate, he does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is specifically when there is an אתרוג for each and every brother. But if the others have only a quince or a pomegranate, he does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבה בר רב הונא's ruling to one kind of situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When every brother has an אתרוג, each one is fully letting the others keep theirs, so each אתרוג can truly belong to the one who holds it. If the others end up with a lesser fruit, the ruling is that he does not fulfill the מצוה. Being allowed to eat it is not enough in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: specifically, only in this case
for each and every one
a quince
a pomegranate

steps.whatToRemember: A brother fulfills the מצוה with an אתרוג bought from shared estate money only if he may eat it and every brother has his own אתרוג.

phrases.english: And this is specifically where there is an אתרוג
for each and every one of the brothers,
but if the others get only a quince or a pomegranate – he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַוְקָא דְּאִיכָּא אֶתְרוֹג לְכׇל חַד וְחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רבה בר רב הונא's ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling that he fulfills the מצוה applies only when each brother has an אתרוג. If the others have only a quince or pomegranate, he does not fulfill it.

steps.title: An אתרוג given on condition that it be returned
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a person who receives an אתרוג as a gift 'on condition that you return it' fulfills his מצוה only if he actually returns it. This teaches that a gift with a condition to return it is still a real gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If someone says, 'This אתרוג is given to you as a gift on condition that you return it to me,' and the person took it and used it for the מצוה: if he returned it, he fulfilled the מצוה; if he did not return it, he did not fulfill it. This teaches us that a gift given on condition that it be returned is called a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling about lending an אתרוג through a 'gift on condition of return.' He also explains what lesson his ruling teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On סוכות you need to own the אתרוג, so a plain loan would not work. רבא says a gift with a return condition is a real gift, so the recipient owns it while he uses it. But the condition matters: if he never returns it, the gift falls apart after the fact, and he never owned it.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that; it sets up a condition attached to a deal
He fulfilled his obligation (here, the מצוה of אתרוג)
It teaches us; this points to the new lesson of a statement
A gift given on condition that it be returned

steps.whatToRemember: A gift on condition of return counts as a real gift. This is how one person can let another use his אתרוג on סוכות, as long as it is actually returned.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a loan. It is a real gift, which is exactly why it works for the מצוה. The condition of returning it is what keeps it from being permanent.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard way people share one אתרוג on the first day of סוכות, when you must own it yourself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: ״אֶתְרוֹג זֶה נָתוּן לְךָ בְּמַתָּנָה,
phrases.english: Rava said: "This etrog is given to you as a gift,
on condition that you return it to me,"
and he took it and fulfilled his obligation with it;
if he returned it, he has fulfilled his obligation;
if he did not return it, he has not fulfilled it.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּמַתָּנָה עַל מְנָת לְהַחֲזִיר –
phrases.english: This teaches us that a gift on condition that it be returned
is called a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: ״אֶתְרוֹג זֶה נָתוּן לְךָ בְּמַתָּנָה, עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּחְזִירֵהוּ לִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of using a gifted or shared אתרוג for the מצוה. It now brings up a new kind of gift that has a condition to return it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג given as a gift on condition of return lets the recipient fulfill the מצוה, but only if he actually returns it. A gift on condition of return is a valid gift.

steps.title: The woman's palm tree and רב ביבי's transfer to his son
steps.stepSummary: A woman owned a palm tree on רב ביבי בר אביי's land. He got upset whenever she came to harvest it, so she gave it to him for his lifetime. He then transferred it to his young son.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain woman who had a palm tree on the land of רב ביבי בר אביי. Whenever she went to cut its fruit, he would get upset at her. So she transferred it to him for all the years of his life. He went and transferred it to his minor son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next step. The question is whether רב ביבי could pass on a tree he was only given for his lifetime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman's gift was limited: it was his only 'for all the years of his life.' After that, it was meant to come back to her. By giving it to his son, רב ביבי tried to keep it in his family even after his death, which would cut off her return.

keyTerms.meaning: A palm tree
He was upset or annoyed
She transferred ownership of it
All the years of his life; a gift for his lifetime only
His minor son

phrases.english: There was a certain woman who had a palm tree
on the land of Rav Beivai bar Abaye.
Whenever she would go to cut its fruit,
he would get upset at her.
She transferred it to him for all the years of his life.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל אִיהוּ אַקְנְיֵיהּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ לִבְנוֹ קָטָן.
phrases.english: He went and transferred it to his minor son.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּהֲוָה לַהּ דִּיקְלָא בְּאַרְעָא דְּרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a gift that must be returned (the אתרוג) to a gift that goes back to the giver after the recipient's lifetime.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real case: a lifetime gift that would go back to the giver, which the recipient then passed on to his son.

steps.title: רב הונא rejects the transfer: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only allows it when the property goes to someone else
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע sharply criticizes רב ביבי. He explains that even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who lets a first recipient sell, only says so when the property is meant to go to another person afterward, not back to the giver.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Because you come from 'cut-short' people, you say 'cut-short' things? Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only said this when the property goes to another person afterward. But when it goes back to the giver himself, he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects what רב ביבי did. He shows that the transfer to his son does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 2 we learned that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets the first recipient sell when the gift says 'to you, and after you to someone else.' רב הונא limits that view. When the gift is supposed to return to the giver herself, she clearly meant to keep her rights, so the recipient cannot sell or give it away.

keyTerms.meaning: From 'cut-short' people; a jab at his family line
'Cut-short' (unsound) words
To another person
To himself, meaning back to the giver

steps.whatToRemember: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets the first recipient sell only when the gift goes to a third person afterward. When it is supposed to return to the giver, the recipient cannot sell or pass it on.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבן שמעון בן גמליאל always lets the first recipient sell. רב הונא limits his view to a gift that goes on to someone else afterward.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Because you come from cut-short people,
you say cut-short words?
phrases.notes: It's a wordplay: his family came from 'cut-short' people, so he jokes that his ideas are 'cut short' too, meaning unsound.

phrases.english: Even Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
phrases.notes: This points back to his view (step 2) that the first recipient can sell the property.

phrases.english: only said this when it goes to another person;
but when it goes back to himself, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּאָתוּ מִמּוּלָאֵי, אָמְרִיתוּ מִילֵּי מוּלְיָאתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the story in step 6 by rejecting רב ביבי's transfer to his son.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ביבי בר אביי's transfer of the palm tree to his son.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He relied on a view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that only applies when the property goes to someone else afterward. Here the property was meant to come back to the giver.

steps.title: An ox given on condition of return that was consecrated and then returned
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: if an ox was given on condition of return, and the recipient made it הקדש and then gave it back, it is both consecrated and returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: If someone says, 'This ox is given to you as a gift on condition that you return it to me,' and the recipient consecrated it and then returned it, it is consecrated and returned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes a ruling of רב נחמן about an ox given on condition of return. The recipient made it הקדש before giving it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a gift on condition of return is a real gift, the recipient truly owns the ox, so his הקדש works. Giving back the consecrated ox still counts as fulfilling the condition, even though the giver can no longer use it for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox
He consecrated it (made it הקדש)
Consecrated; it belongs to הקדש
Returned; the condition is fulfilled

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, a gift on condition of return gives full ownership. The recipient can even make it הקדש, and returning it still fulfills the condition. But רבא challenges this right away in step 9, and in step 11 רב אשי rules that with the words 'return it to me', as in this case, the condition is not met.

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
"This ox is given to you as a gift,
on condition that you return it to me";
if he consecrated it and returned it,
it is consecrated and returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: ״שׁוֹר זֶה נָתוּן לְךָ בְּמַתָּנָה, עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּחְזִירֵהוּ לִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the topic of step 5, a gift on condition of return, and applies it to an ox that was made הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox given on condition of return, then consecrated and returned by the recipient, is both consecrated and considered returned.

steps.title: רבא asks what was really returned
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: if the ox is הקדש, what did the recipient actually give back?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: What did he return to him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling from Step 8. He asks how the condition of return can count as kept when the ox now belongs to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ox is הקדש, the original owner cannot use it or treat it as his own. So רבא argues that handing back a consecrated ox is not a real return, and the condition was never fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he return to him?
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
What did he return to him?
phrases.notes: He means a consecrated ox isn't really the owner's anymore, so nothing true was given back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: מַאי אַהְדְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the ox is both consecrated and returned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A consecrated ox is useless to the giver, so returning it does not fulfill the condition of return.

steps.title: רב נחמן answers that nothing was lost
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן replies: what did the giver lose? He got his ox back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And what did he cause him to lose?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling. He says the condition only required giving the ox back, and the ox was given back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads the condition simply: the giver asked for the ox to come back, and it physically came back. In his view, the condition did not require the ox to come back usable.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did he cause him to lose?

phrases.english: He said to him:
And what did he cause him to lose?
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is answering here: the ox itself came back, so the giver is missing nothing he asked for.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the premise of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Returning a consecrated ox is not a real return
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition only asked for the ox back, and it was returned

steps.title: רב אשי says it depends on the exact wording
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי distinguishes: 'on condition that you return it' is fulfilled, but 'return it to me' requires something the giver can use.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: We look at what was said. If he said 'on condition that you return it,' he returned it. If he said 'on condition that you return it to me,' he meant something fit for his use.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי settles the argument between רבא and רב נחמן by making the outcome depend on the exact words the giver used. In the case as it was actually stated ('return it to me'), he agrees with רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain 'return it' only requires giving the item back, so a consecrated ox counts as returned. Adding 'to me' shows the giver wanted something he could use, so a consecrated ox fails the condition, as רבא argued. רב נחמן's own case used the words 'return it to me,' so in that exact case the condition is not met, and both the gift and the הקדש fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: We look and see (it depends on the case)
On condition that you return it
Something fit for him to use

steps.whatToRemember: A condition to return a gift is judged by its exact words. 'Return it' is met by any return. 'Return it to me' needs something the giver can use.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that small changes in the wording of a condition can change the הלכה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
We see (what was said);
If he said to him: "On condition that you return it"
– he has returned it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּחְזִירֵהוּ לִי״
phrases.english: If he said to him: "On condition that you return it to me"
– he was telling him (to return) something fit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the back-and-forth between רבא and רב נחמן by splitting the cases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two wordings of the condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One rule applies to every condition of return
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Return it' is fulfilled by any return; 'return it to me' requires a usable item

steps.title: שמואל says a refusing recipient still acquires
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if someone writes his property to another person, the recipient acquires it even if he loudly refuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If one writes his property to another, and the other says 'I do not want it,' he acquires it, even if he stands and shouts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: gifts that the recipient refuses. שמואל says the gift takes effect anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, once the giver writes the property over, ownership passes right away. The recipient's later protest does not undo it, no matter how strongly he objects.

keyTerms.meaning: One who writes his property to another
I do not want them
Standing and shouting (in protest)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One who writes his property to another,
phrases.notes: He means writing a document that gives the property to the other person.

phrases.english: and the other one said "I do not want them"
– he acquires,
and even if he stands and shouts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַכּוֹתֵב נְכָסָיו לְאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of conditional gifts ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A recipient of written property acquires it even if he protests

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says he does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: a recipient who refuses does not acquire the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: He does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite ruling from שמואל. The refusal stops the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, a gift needs the recipient to go along with it. If he says he does not want it, the property does not become his.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not acquire

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
He does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to שמואל in Step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A recipient who refuses the gift does not acquire it

steps.title: רבי אבא בר ממל says they do not disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל begins to explain that שמואל and רבי יוחנן do not really argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said: And they do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבי אבא בר ממל says the two rulings can fit together, and his explanation comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of treating שמואל and רבי יוחנן as opposing views, he is about to show that each one is talking about a different situation. We have to wait for the next lines to see how he splits the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said:
And they do not disagree;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a reconciliation of שמואל and רבי יוחנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל and רבי יוחנן's rulings do not truly conflict (explanation follows)
